meanings.note: About people. Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'брый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('kind; good').
in greetings: добрый день, добрый вечер

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

examples.text: Я вчера ел маринованные грибы. Может, один гриб был плохой.
examples.trans: Yesterday I ate pickled mushrooms. Maybe one mushroom was bad.

meanings.note: Opposite of открытый. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'крытый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('closed').

examples.trans: I declare the court session closed.

meanings.note: Second in command. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'меститель'). Agent/instrument noun formed with the productive Slavic suffix '-тель' ('-er'). Common masculine noun meaning 'deputy' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The new mayor is Anikeev's deputy.

meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
Parenthetical. Core Russian adv meaning 'so, then, that means' in everyday speech.
verb: Что это значит? = What does it mean?
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: в кухне / на кухне = in the kitchen, на кухню = to the kitchen
E.g. русская кухня. Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).

examples.trans: And the kitchen is over there.
We are sitting in the kitchen.

examples.text: Проходите, пожалуйста! Как видите, большой коридор, а там кухня.
examples.trans: Come on in, please! As you can see, a big hall, and the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Head of a town. Borrowed from French 'maire' (from Latin 'maior', greater/senior official).

examples.text: Я уже четыре года работаю мэром.
examples.trans: I've been working as mayor for four years now.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'кормить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to feed'.

examples.trans: The cook fed the guests deliciously.

examples.text: Раз не можем напоить, мы его накормим!
examples.trans: Since we cannot give him drink, we will feed him!

examples.text: Мы накормим его вкусным горячим обедом.
examples.trans: We will feed him a delicious hot lunch.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не будет командовать на моей кухне!

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?

But legally you are nobody to her.

meanings.note: Понял? = got it?; понял = got it. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to understand', paired with 'понимать'.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Вот он, телефон! Сами решайте, что делать. Без меня!

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'правляющий'). Common masculine noun meaning 'manager' in everyday Russian.

meanings.note: Put in order or set up. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'страивать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to organize, arrange', paired with 'устроить'.

meanings.note: + infinitive or a noun. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to want', paired with 'захотеть'.
